Changes in your body during pregnancy aren't limited to a growing belly. While many women enjoy thicker hair during this period, an increase in hair ("hirsutism") not just on the head, but also on the face, abdomen, and other unwanted areas can be an unpleasant surprise.

The desire for smooth skin grows, especially in the summer months or as childbirth approaches. If you started laser hair removal before pregnancy, it's natural to want to continue. But are these "miracle rays" safe for your baby? Why are cosmetologists hesitant to accept pregnant clients?

Let's explore the medical facts and risks surrounding laser hair removal.Do laser rays reach the baby?

First, let's dispel the fear of "radiation." The rays used in laser hair removal (Alexandrite, Diode, Nd:YAG) are **non-ionizing** radiation. This means they do not have the power to change cell structure (DNA) like X-rays or CT scans.  - **Depth:** Laser rays penetrate only a few millimeters into the skin (down to the hair follicle).
  - **The Truth:** It is physically impossible for these rays to pass through muscles, enter the uterus, and directly touch the fetus.Nevertheless, most doctors and dermatologists worldwide recommend **abstaining** from laser during pregnancy. But why?Why "Waiting" is the best decision?

Although no direct harm from lasers has been proven, there are very serious reasons not to have this procedure during pregnancy:1. Lack of Research

Science never conducts risky experiments on pregnant women and babies. There are no large-scale clinical studies on the safety of lasers during pregnancy. The phrase "not proven" can mean both "harmless" and "could be harmful." The golden rule in medicine: **When in doubt, don't.**2. Hormonal "Chaos" and Risk of Staining

Melanin (pigment) production increases during pregnancy. This means your skin is more sensitive to light and heat.  - **Risk:** Laser rays can cause permanent burns or **hyperpigmentation** (dark spots) on the skin. Also, due to hormonal influence, your hair may not "obey" the laser—meaning you might be wasting your money.3. Pain and Stress Factor

Laser can be painful, especially in sensitive areas (bikini, underarms). During pregnancy, your pain threshold drops.  - **Danger:** Sharp pain or fear releases adrenaline in the body. This can cause **uterine tone** (contractions), which is undesirable for the course of pregnancy.So, which methods are safe?

Even if you take a break from the laser, you don't have to go ungroomed. Alternatives you can use during pregnancy:✅ Razor (Britva) – The Safest

An old but reliable friend. It contains no chemicals or radiation.  - **Tip:** As your belly grows, it may be difficult to see your lower limbs. Be careful or ask your partner for help.🟡 Sugaring and Waxing (Epilation) – Conditional

If you used these methods before pregnancy and are used to the pain, you can continue.  - **Attention:** Blood vessels dilate during pregnancy. Hot wax or harsh pulling can damage **varicose** veins. Also, pay special attention to hygiene (risk of infection).🟡 Depilatory Creams – With Caution

Although the chemicals in them (barium sulfide, etc.) are absorbed into the blood in minute amounts, the main problem is their sharp smell.  - **Tip:** If you have toxicoses, the smell may cause nausea. Always do an allergy test (on a small part of your arm) before use.When can you return to the laser?

You can resume laser procedures after you hold your baby in your arms.  - **Breastfeeding:** Laser rays do not pass into milk and do not affect the mammary glands (even during underarm epilation). Laser is considered safe for breastfeeding mothers.
  - **However:** Waiting 3-6 months after birth for hormones to fully normalize will ensure more effective results.The saying "beauty requires sacrifice" does not apply to pregnancy. Now the main priority is your comfort and your baby's safety. Laser hair removal isn't going anywhere; it will be waiting for you in 9 months.

For now, prioritize the safest and most stress-free methods. To check your skin's sensitivity and the status of other procedures (e.g., hair dyeing), take a look at the **"Safety Database" in the Anacan app**.
